100.question: What does NBA stand for?
100.explanation: The National Basketball Association was formed in 1949 and is the top professional basketball league in North America.

200.question: What earlier league merged with the NBL to form the NBA's direct predecessor structure?
200.explanation: The Basketball Association of America (BAA), founded in 1946, merged with the National Basketball League (NBL) in 1949 to form the NBA.

300.question: What team won many early NBA titles after relocating from Minneapolis to Los Angeles?
300.explanation: The Lakers won five early NBA titles in Minneapolis, then moved to Los Angeles in 1960 and kept their name, even though Los Angeles has few lakes.

400.question: What dominant big man led the Minneapolis Lakers to several early championships?
400.explanation: George Mikan, a 6-foot-10 center, was the league's first dominant big man. He led the Minneapolis Lakers to five championships.

500.question: What rule introduced in 1954 forced teams to attempt a shot within a set time?
500.explanation: The 24-second shot clock, adopted in 1954, ended slow stalling games and sped up play. Scoring jumped right away.

100.question: What Boston Celtics center won 11 NBA championships as a player?
100.explanation: Bill Russell won 11 championships in his 13 seasons with the Celtics, the most of any player in NBA history.

200.question: What player scored 100 points in a single NBA game in 1962?
200.explanation: Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks on March 2, 1962, an NBA record that still stands.

300.question: What Celtics coach led Boston during much of its 1950s and 1960s dynasty?
300.explanation: Red Auerbach coached the Celtics to nine championships, including eight in a row from 1959 to 1966, and was known for lighting a victory cigar.

400.question: What guard was known as The Logo and starred for the Lakers in the 1960s?
400.explanation: Jerry West's silhouette is widely believed to be the model for the NBA logo, which earned him the nickname The Logo.

500.question: What player averaged a triple-double for the 1961-62 season?
500.explanation: Oscar Robertson averaged a triple-double for the 1961-62 season: 30.8 points, 12.5 rebounds, and 11.4 assists per game.

100.question: What rival basketball league merged with the NBA in 1976?
100.explanation: The American Basketball Association merged with the NBA in 1976. Four ABA teams joined: the Nuggets, Pacers, Nets, and Spurs.

200.question: What flashy ABA and NBA star was nicknamed Dr. J?
200.explanation: Julius Erving, Dr. J, brought high-flying dunks to the ABA and NBA and won a championship with the Philadelphia 76ers in 1983.

300.question: What team won the 1977 NBA Finals behind Bill Walton?
300.explanation: Bill Walton led the Portland Trail Blazers past the Philadelphia 76ers for the 1977 title and was named Finals MVP.

400.question: What team won the 1979 NBA championship led by Dennis Johnson and Jack Sikma?
400.explanation: The Seattle SuperSonics beat the Washington Bullets in the 1979 Finals for the franchise's only title. Dennis Johnson was Finals MVP.

500.question: What feature from the ABA later became a major part of NBA basketball strategy?
500.explanation: The ABA used a three-point line from its start in 1967. The NBA adopted it in 1979, and today the three-pointer is central to the game.

100.question: What Lakers point guard led the Showtime offense in the 1980s?
100.explanation: Magic Johnson ran the fast-breaking Showtime Lakers and won five championships in the 1980s.

200.question: What Celtics forward was Magic Johnson's famous rival during the 1980s?
200.explanation: Larry Bird led the Celtics to three titles in the 1980s. His rivalry with Magic Johnson, which began in college, helped revive the NBA's popularity.

300.question: What Lakers center was famous for the skyhook?
300.explanation: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's nearly unstoppable skyhook made him the NBA's all-time leading scorer for almost 39 years.

400.question: What Detroit Pistons teams were known for their physical Bad Boys style?
400.explanation: The Bad Boys Pistons, led by Isiah Thomas and Bill Laimbeer, used tough, physical defense to win back-to-back titles in 1989 and 1990.

500.question: What coach led the Lakers to multiple championships during the Showtime era?
500.explanation: Pat Riley coached the Showtime Lakers to four championships in the 1980s and later won another as coach of the Miami Heat.

100.question: What Chicago Bulls player became the defining star of the 1990s NBA?
100.explanation: Michael Jordan led the Bulls to six titles in the 1990s, winning Finals MVP every time, and became a global icon.

200.question: What Bulls coach led Chicago to six NBA championships in the 1990s?
200.explanation: Phil Jackson coached the Bulls to six titles with his triangle offense, then won five more with the Lakers, for 11 in total.

300.question: What Bulls forward was Jordan's longtime star teammate?
300.explanation: Scottie Pippen, a versatile forward and elite defender, was Jordan's teammate for all six Bulls championships.

400.question: What Houston Rockets center led the team to back-to-back titles in 1994 and 1995?
400.explanation: Hakeem Olajuwon, famous for his Dream Shake post moves, led the Houston Rockets to titles in 1994 and 1995 while Jordan was away from the Bulls.

500.question: What Utah Jazz duo repeatedly challenged the Bulls in the late 1990s Finals?
500.explanation: Karl Malone and John Stockton, masters of the pick-and-roll, led the Utah Jazz to the 1997 and 1998 Finals, losing both to the Bulls.

100.question: What Lakers star was nicknamed the Black Mamba?
100.explanation: Kobe Bryant, the Black Mamba, spent his whole 20-year career with the Lakers and won five championships.

200.question: What Spurs power forward was nicknamed The Big Fundamental?
200.explanation: Tim Duncan's simple, flawless technique earned him the nickname The Big Fundamental. He won five titles with the Spurs.

300.question: What player led the Cleveland Cavaliers to their first NBA championship in 2016?
300.explanation: LeBron James led the Cavaliers back from a 3-1 deficit against the Golden State Warriors in 2016 to win Cleveland's first NBA title.

400.question: What Warriors guard helped transform the NBA with high-volume three-point shooting?
400.explanation: Stephen Curry's deep, high-volume three-point shooting changed how teams play. He holds the NBA record for career three-pointers made.

500.question: What Denver Nuggets center won Finals MVP after leading Denver to its first NBA title in 2023?
500.explanation: Nikola Jokic, a center known for elite passing, led the Nuggets past the Miami Heat in 2023 and was named Finals MVP.
